message: The rotation transform is added to a renderer that the main web application does not use. At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, apps/web/src/app.tsx:48-65 registers createDomRendererPlugin() and createGpuRendererPlugin(); packages/dom-renderer/src/plugin.tsx:22-31 renders DomShapeLayer, whose wrapper has no rotation transform (packages/dom-renderer/src/dom-shape-layer.tsx:24-34). GPU rendering likewise constructs axis-aligned vertices without applying rotation (packages/gpu-renderer/src/shaders/shape-sdf.ts:33-55). Consequently, shapes remain visually unrotated in the application while the newly wrapped hit tests use rotated geometry: visible portions can become unclickable and empty regions selectable. Apply rotation to the active DOM renderer and implement GPU rotation or leave rotated shapes to a rotation-capable DOM fallback.

At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, the double-click listener still calls the raw hitTest(shape, event.worldPoint), although registration now uses withRotation(hitTest) at line 270. Thus selection and text-edit activation disagree about which points belong to rotated text. For example, a 200×28 text shape rotated 90 degrees cannot enter editing by double-clicking its visible ends outside the original horizontal bounds. The editing machine requires successive POINTER_DOWN events identifying the same shape (plugins/usketch-plugin-shape-text/src/text-editing-machine.ts:79-100), but this listener reports null there. Use the rotation-aware hit test in the editing listener as well.

At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, sticky-note double-click detection invokes the unwrapped hitTest directly, bypassing the rotation-aware registered hit test. For a note rotated 45 degrees, clicks on visible corners outside its original bounds do not send POINTER_DOWN to the editing service, so double-clicking those areas cannot enter editing even when selection correctly identifies the note. The editing transition requires two clicks identifying the same shape (this file:166-188). Reuse withRotation(hitTest), or the registered shape hit test, in this listener.

The name searches treat an empty first files.list page as definitive absence without requesting or following nextPageToken. Drive permits empty intermediate pages, so findFolderByName can return null for an existing folder and findOrCreateFolder then creates a duplicate. getAppDataFileByName has the same defect at lines 165–172 and can incorrectly throw DriveNotFoundError for existing JSON data. Request nextPageToken and continue searching until a match is found or pagination is exhausted.

Drive's HTTP 403 dailyLimitExceeded reason is missing from the quota-reason allowlist. Its standard 'Daily Limit Exceeded' message also does not match the 'rate limit' fallback, so daily API quota exhaustion becomes DrivePermissionError instead of DriveQuotaExceededError. Consumers consequently cannot distinguish exhausted API quota from missing access permissions. Include dailyLimitExceeded in the quota classification while preserving the original HTTP status.

The name searches treat an empty first page as proof that the resource does not exist, without requesting or following nextPageToken. Drive files.list can return empty partial pages even when subsequent pages contain matches. Consequently, findOrCreateFolder can create a duplicate folder instead of reusing an existing one. getAppDataFileByName has the same defect at lines 165–172 and can incorrectly throw DriveNotFoundError for existing JSON data. Request nextPageToken and continue searching until a match is found or pagination is exhausted. Evidence: src/lib/drive-client.ts at revision 876934a63ff912a060320102a818b48476a59136, lines 160–178 and 368–389.

The quota-reason allowlist omits Drive's dailyLimitExceeded and storageQuotaExceeded reasons. A 403 response with either reason and its normal message falls through to DrivePermissionError because the message does not contain 'rate limit'. Callers therefore cannot distinguish exhausted daily quota or full Drive storage from insufficient permissions, undermining the promised quota-error handling and leading to the wrong recovery action. Include these quota reasons in the classification. Evidence: src/lib/drive-errors.ts at revision 876934a63ff912a060320102a818b48476a59136, lines 59–80.

The new version lookup makes publishing a NOT_BUILT result depend on a successful /version request. If that request fails—for example, with a transient 502 or 503—retryOnServerError propagates the exception before createCommitStatus is attempted. JobCompletedListener only logs the failure, so an existing pending status is never replaced even if the commit-status endpoint is available. Previously this result could be published as WARNING without querying the version. Catch version-discovery failures and fall back to WARNING when SKIPPED support cannot be established.

The version lookup is now a prerequisite for publishing any NOT_BUILT status, but there is no fallback if that request fails. If /api/v1/version times out or returns an HTTP error even while the commit-status endpoint remains available, the exception escapes sendNotifications and JobCompletedListener only logs it (head 2e021e56de9104d8d124cac086cf6b208b6b4a88, lines 342–348). No terminal status is posted, potentially leaving the completed build marked pending indefinitely. Previously, NOT_BUILT published WARNING without this request (base 19c54c3e5d9cc19d47302688526d1b016dd2110d, lines 109–111). Fall back to WARNING when the capability lookup fails rather than dropping the notification.

The new API-key methods pass credential-bearing responses through requestV3, which logs the entire parsed response when debug is enabled. createApiKey therefore writes the generated data.key to stdout, and listApiKeys similarly logs all returned keys. This exposes usable account credentials to anyone with access to collected diagnostic logs. Redact key values before logging or suppress response-body logging for these endpoints. Evidence: src/client.ts at HEAD 550f7bc03fbc4e1760f9f4f4382cd612f7aeedf8, lines 186–190 (console logging), 293–301 (unredacted response logging), and 1807–1829 (the new API-key calls).

The new API-key endpoints send credential-bearing responses through requestV3(), which logs the entire response without redaction. When debug is enabled, createApiKey() writes the newly generated key to stdout, and listApiKeys() similarly exposes the returned keys. These credentials can consequently reach centralized logs and become accessible to log readers. Redact key values or suppress response-body logging for API-key endpoints. Evidence at HEAD 550f7bc03fbc4e1760f9f4f4382cd612f7aeedf8: src/client.ts:180-189 (console logging), 293-300 (unredacted response logging), and 1807-1829 (new endpoint calls).
